title: Unconscionability
summary: Unconscionability examines whether the circumstances of agreement and the substance of its terms make enforcement impermissibly unfair under the governing rule.
notes:
Williams considers meaningful choice together with terms unreasonably favorable to the seller. The purchase documents allowed earlier purchases to remain subject to repossession through a cross-collateral arrangement, and the court remanded for the relevant assessment rather than itself awarding final relief. Stoll examines a transaction involving language difficulties and a chicken-litter provision whose consequences dwarfed the nominal land-price adjustment.

Procedural concerns include how terms were presented and the parties’ opportunities to understand and choose. Substantive concerns include the obligations and risks imposed. Their required relationship and the remedy depend on governing law. Graham separately evaluates a biased arbitration arrangement. A harsh term, unequal bargaining position, or disappointing result should be connected to the particular legal standard rather than treated as self-proving.

The supplied Anderson opinion is assigned alongside these materials, but its actual analysis of notice, amendment, and accrued claims should be preserved rather than rewritten as a generic unconscionability holding.

topics.unconscionability: Enforceability depends on the relevant procedural and substantive concerns.
